data.name: Adalyn
data.gender_notes: Adalyn is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old High German elements adal, meaning 'noble,' and lyn, meaning 'maiden, lion, or linnet (a type of bird). The name Adalyn can be interpreted as 'noble little lion' or 'noble maiden,' emphasizing the strength and courage within a feminine form. The name Adalyn carries the meaning “Noble, noblewoman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Adalyn usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, noblewoman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Adalyn belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, noblewoman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adalyn total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

It symbolizes the power and resilience of a woman who stands firm against the adversities of life, inspiring others with her unwavering spirit. Adalyn's spiritual meaning can also serve as a reminder for individuals to tap into their own inner strength and courage when faced with challenges or hardships.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adalyn: Noble, Kind, and Bright as a Noble-Noble-hearted one (Noble-Adah) and a Dark-light (Dark-Lyn). Her name is a reflection of her strong character and radiant spirit.

historical_references.reference: Adalyn is derived from the Old Norse name 'Adalhildr'. This name is believed to have meant 'noble and bright'. The Viking Age, encompassing the late 8th to late 11th centuries, was the period during which Old Norse names like Adalhildr were in use in Scandinavia and among the Norse settlers in the British Isles.
historical_references.context: Old Norse names and Scandinavian culture

historical_references.reference: The name Adalyn gained Christian connotations during the Middle Ages when it was associated with Saint Adalyn, a legendary Irish saint who was said to have been the daughter of a king. According to the legend, she was martyred along with her seven brothers in County Wexford, Ireland, during the 6th century. The name Adalyn became popular among Christians as a result of this saint's story.
